1.3: 1.3 Of all the men. ORIGEN, Homily 1 on Numbers. Otherwise the Septuagint: Everyone who goes forth in the strength of Israel, etc. He therefore who goes forth, etc., up to is handed down through evangelical and apostolic faith.
1.4: 1.4 The leaders of the tribes, etc. AUGUSTINE, Questions on Numbers 1. Why does he command that a leader be chosen from each of the tribes, etc., up to that they may be called.
1.5: 1.5 Of the tribe of Reuben. RABANUS on Numbers, vol. 2. Morally, Reuben, the firstborn of Israel, etc., up to one heart and one soul. RABANUS, ibid. The leader of the tribe of Reuben signifies in general those, etc., up to having care of the continent, of virgins, and of both sexes.
1.6: 1.6 Of the tribe of Simeon. RABANUS. Simeon signifies in general all the obedient, etc., up to saying: To you I have lifted up my eyes, you who dwell in the heavens Ps. 122.
1.7: 1.7 Of the tribe of Judah. THE SAME. In Judah can be signified all who rightly call upon the name of the Lord, dissenting from the rule of faith neither in thought nor in word. Of these Nahshon is rightly the leader, who not only instructs others by preaching, but also slays within himself the poisonous darts of the vices by chastising his body, according to that saying: I chastise my body and bring it into subjection, etc. 1 Cor. 9. Allegorically, Judah, from whom the kings come, whose name is interpreted confession or praise, here signifies the people of the Church, whose head is the lion of the tribe of Judah, that is, Christ. For truly the praise or confession of faith, that is, right preaching, is only in the Church. Nahshon, therefore, that is, serpentine, or augury, the son of Amminadab, that is, of the willing people, is understood to be the Savior, begotten of the patriarchs, the servants devoted to God, who by his death destroyed the devil. For in the serpent, from which the cause of death first came, that is, sin, death is prefigured. Hence: As Moses lifted up the serpent in the desert, so must the Son of Man be lifted up, etc. John 3.
1.8: 1.8 Of the tribe of Issachar. THE SAME. Issachar fittingly expresses the monks, who, having scorned all the affairs of the world, by the gift of God, that is, under the protection of the Holy Spirit, seek the eternal reward by a strict life and by mortified pleasure, and, trampling on the pomp of the world and embracing lowly things, desire to please God alone. Nethanel son of Zuar. Of those who devoutly exert themselves to receive a reward in heaven, the leader is Nethanel, that is, my God or gift of God, son of Zuar, that is, of the little ones of Christ, namely of him who appeared little among men: for he is himself both the leader and the reward.
1.9: 1.9 Of the tribe of Zebulun. THE SAME. Zebulun represents the patient, etc., up to namely against heretics and schismatics.
1.10: 1.10 Joseph. The same Joseph, father of two tribes, signifies Christ, the Father of two peoples and the cornerstone. Ephraim the younger, set before Manasseh the firstborn, signifies the Gentile people set before the Jewish. Hence: Amen I say to you, I have not found such great faith in Israel Matt. 8. Elishama. Elishama signifies Christ, of whom it is said: He became obedient to the Father unto death, etc. Phil. 2. He says of himself: The things I have heard from him, these I speak in the world John 8. He is the son of Ammihud, that is, of the renowned people, namely of the stock of kings, patriarchs and prophets. RABANUS. Elishama, leader in the tribe of Ephraim, signifies those who attentively hear the word of God with a good and excellent heart, and bear fruit in patience. Manasseh, etc. Forgetful, namely forgetting the things that are behind and stretching forward to those ahead, that he may receive the crown of life, which God will give to those who love him Phil. 3; James 1. Gamaliel. Gamaliel, God has repaid me, son of Pedahzur, that is, of mighty redemption, is leader in the tribe of Manasseh, which is interpreted forgotten, or forgetful, since Christ, whom the Father sent into the world to call the Jewish people, found in his kingdom a forgetful nation. For Israel forgot its Creator. Yet not all perished, but when the fullness of the Gentiles has come in, all Israel will be saved Rom. 11.
1.11: 1.11 Of the tribe of Benjamin. Benjamin signifies Jerusalem, which is in his tribe. Its people, according to the prophecy of Rachel, was Ben-oni, that is, son of sorrow, because it afflicted its mother with grievous sorrow. For it shed the blood of the prophets, and, conspiring in the killing of Christ, said: His blood be upon us and upon our children Matt. 27. But in believers, according to the father's prophecy, it is the son of the right hand. Benjamin can also signify the Gentile people, who were a son of sorrow by persecuting Christians. He may also be called son of the right hand, because at the judgment he will be at God's right hand, or because he does the right hand, that is, good works. The leader of this people is Abidan, that is, my father is judge, son of Gideoni, which is interpreted temptation of iniquity or of humility; for Christ, whom the Jew despised as lowly and the devil unjustly tempted, is the head of believers and the judge to come of the living and the dead. Morally, Benjamin, son of the right hand, signifies those who fight bravely against their enemies, and bravely suppress the goads of temptation, and allow nothing womanish or soft to rule in them.
1.12: 1.12 Of the tribe of Dan. Dan means judgment, or judging. These are the ones who do everything with discernment, who appoint Ahiezer, that is, brother and helper, as their leader: because they do all things according to the rule of the Fathers, or attribute all their good things to God. RABANUS, as above. Dan, etc., up to they exhort to fellowship in spiritual grace.
1.13: 1.13 Of the tribe of Asher. THE SAME. Asher, etc., up to for they will be repaid in the resurrection of the just.
1.14: 1.14 Of the tribe of Gad. THE SAME. Allegorically, etc., up to hence: The cock girded about the loins, and the ram, and there is no king who can resist him Prov. 30.
1.15: 1.15 Of the tribe of Naphtali. Naphtali, etc., up to hence: No longer do I call you servants, but friends, etc. John 15.
1.16: 1.16 By their families. AUGUSTINE, Questions on Numbers 2. It is rightly asked why, etc., up to and the new by the four Gospels.
1.18: 1.18 From twenty years old. ISIDORE. Those chosen for war are counted from the twentieth year, because from this age wars arise against each one's vices. And so they are chosen for battle, that they may fight against lust, lest they be overcome by luxury.
1.37: 1.37 Thirty-five thousand. The good married, because to signify thirty the index finger and thumb are joined in a gentle kiss. Hence one fruit is thirtyfold, another sixtyfold, another a hundredfold.
1.51: 1.51 And when they must set out, etc. That is, by word and example they will arrange how each, humbled, may advance in progress in the virtues. Whoever of outsiders, etc. AUGUSTINE, Question 3. The stranger who approaches shall die. Here the stranger is to be understood also of those sons of Israel, etc., up to so that they are called allophyli, as if men of other tribes. Allegorically. He who approaches the sacred ministry unworthily does not escape the penalty of presumption: for no one ought to take the honor upon himself, except one who is called by God, as Aaron was Heb. 5. Hence Uzziah, who usurped the priesthood, was struck with leprosy.
1.52: 1.52 Each by their companies, etc. ORIGEN, Homily 2 on Numbers. Each according to their own signs, etc., up to if nothing restless, nothing disordered, nothing dishonorable is found in us.
1.54: 1.54 Seven hundred. Those advanced in spiritual gifts, to be placed at God's right hand. For the number one hundred is first reckoned on the right hand, with the thumb and index finger bent into a circle; hence: Now his right hand counts the years. RABANUS on Numbers, vol. 2. In the tribe of Levi, etc., up to as if on their shoulders of labor and patience they carry the Church.
2.1: 2.1 And the Lord spoke. ORIGEN, Homily 2 on Numbers. A man according to his own order, etc., up to and to do nothing according to order. THE SAME. Each one of us, etc., up to lest because of him the name of God be blasphemed. THE SAME. According to their own signs, etc. By which, namely, the character of each is designated, etc., up to how much more do the rest of men bear their own signs in the movements of their minds and the powers of the soul?
2.2: 2.2 Around the tabernaculum, etc. RABANUS on Numbers. Around the tabernacle, etc., up to by whose prayers and teaching the Church is fortified.
2.9: 2.9 All who were in the camp of Judah. Over these tribes Judah presides, namely the royal tribe, from which Christ arose, king and savior of the human race.
2.10: 2.10 On the southern side the leader will be. This signifies the ancient people of God, who, receiving the light of the Gospel, or of the law, burned with love of the Creator.
2.17: 2.17 And the tabernacle of the testimony shall be taken up, etc. The raising or taking down of the tabernacle signifies the condition of the Church, which is raised up in believers and taken down in deniers, is exalted in certain holy orders, and in others is humbled by the judgment of the priests through excommunication. On the west side they shall be, etc. RABANUS on Numbers, vol. 2. Let us say something further that may help the reader, etc., up to so that they may securely fulfill the divine office.
2.18: 2.18 On the west. This side, receiving into itself both walls of the tabernacle, completes them by joining them, and signifies the consummation of the Church at the end of the world, when the elect will be approved in the fruit of good works, the wicked will be handed over to the oblivion of death, and the just will be placed at God's right hand.
2.25: 2.25 The sons of Dan encamped on the north side. This side signifies the multitude of the nations, until Christ numb with the cold of unbelief, but, the Jews having been rejected by God's judgment, expecting eternal blessedness in the Church once it is spread abroad.
3.3: 3.3 Of the priests who were anointed, etc. RABANUS on Numbers, vol. 2. The four sons of Aaron, etc., up to are consumed by the fire of divine vengeance.
3.6: 3.6 Bring near the tribe. AUGUSTINE, Question 4 on Numbers. Take the tribe of Levi, etc., up to in the other camps round about of the children of Israel.
3.10: 3.10 The outsider. THE SAME. The stranger who touches it shall die. It must be asked how he said, etc., up to for it was of this that he was speaking.
3.12: 3.12 I have taken the Levites. THE SAME, Question 6. What is it that the Levites, etc., up to and that the descendants of the Levites or of their cattle are not counted for these. ORIGEN, Homily 3 on Numbers. I have taken the Levites from the midst of the children of Israel for every firstborn, etc. The Levites are taken for the firstborn, etc., up to so that it is more to be taken as a firstborn than to be born a firstborn. The Septuagint: From the midst of the children of Israel, etc. Levi is the third among the sons of Israel; from what midst, then, are the Levites taken? I find the Shunammite confidently answering the king of Israel: I dwell in the midst of my people 2 Kings 4. And John saying of Christ: In the midst of you stands one whom you do not know. I think, then, that he who never turned aside to the right or to the left can be said to stand in the midst, he who did no sin, nor was deceit found in his mouth Isa. 53. And because he always stands, he is said to stand in the midst. But he who is his imitator, like the Shunammite, is indeed not said to stand, because at times he inclines to the right or to the left, for no one is clean from filth, not even if his life were of one day Job 15; yet he is said to dwell in the midst of the people. The Levites, then, are taken from the midst of the children of Israel. For the Levites are those who did not know their right hand and their left, but following Moses, that is, the law of God, did not spare father or mother. And you too, if, when temptation and the anger of sin come, you incline neither to the right nor to the left, do not transgress the law of God, but stand in the midst, fixed and steady, and do not bend your knees to sin, nor follow the head of the beast, that is, the image of folly: you will be taken from the midst of the children of Israel and be placed in the number of the firstfruits. Opens. Not everyone who has opened the womb is worthy of primacy; hence: Sinners are estranged from the womb, they have gone astray from the belly, they have spoken false things Ps. 57. For how could anyone go astray from the way of God as soon as he came out of his mother's womb? Or how could a newborn child speak false things? It is necessary, then, to seek such a belly and womb as can fit: Sinners are estranged from the womb, etc. And that will be the womb that every firstborn who is sanctified to the Lord opens. The Lord opened the womb of Leah, which was closed, and she bore patriarchs; likewise also Rachel, that she too might bear, she whose sight was keen and whose appearance was comely Gen. 29, 30. In many places of Scripture you will find wombs opened; if you consider them one by one by place, you will find how sinners go astray from the womb, and others who open the womb are sanctified in the order of the firstfruits. From the time. ORIGEN. Because the firstborn of Israel had not been sanctified before, etc., up to and might place him in the order of the firstfruits.
3.15: 3.15 Number the sons of Levi. THE SAME. Let us review more attentively, etc., up to and with perpetual watches they celebrate the divine ministries.
3.17: 3.17 Levi by his names. Levi means added or taken up. This is the order of teachers, who, chosen out of the world by the grace of God for divine service, are united to the assemblies of the angels. Hence: I have chosen you out of the world John 15. And elsewhere: But they are as the angels of God in heaven Matt. 22. Gershon and Kohath and Merari. The three sons of Levi signify the preachers of the holy Trinity, distinguished by confession, wonderful in faith, hope and charity. Nor does the interpretation of their names in any way contradict this exposition, but agrees with it well. For Gershon is interpreted stranger, Kohath patience, or molar teeth, Merari bitter, or bitterness; for the minister of God knows himself a stranger and pilgrim in the world, and is patient. He grinds the word of God with the tooth of discernment, according to the capacities of the hearers; and, showing the world to be bitter to himself, calls others back from pleasures. These are numbered from one month old, because they ought to consecrate the beginning of their life to God, lest, promoted after many crimes, they cause the name of God to be blasphemed; hence: A bishop must be blameless, etc. 1 Tim. 3.
3.23: 3.23 These shall be stationed behind the tabernacle. The fitting order of the sons of Levi is shown, namely that those who are first in rank keep the eastern side: Moses and Aaron with their sons having the custody of the sanctuary in the midst of the children of Israel. The Kohathites, from whom Moses and Aaron sprang, hold the southern side, under the care of Eleazar the priest, who is the eldest of the sons of Aaron. After these the Gershonites are on the western side under the care of Eliasaph. Last the Merarites on the northern side, under the custody of Ithamar, the younger son of Aaron. In these is morally expressed that the ministers of the Church ought diligently to keep their own order, and not seek greater things than their own place demands.
3.24: 3.24 On the west under the leader Eliasaph son of Lael. Where the day closes, the stars set. In these is signified that the ministers of the tabernacle ought to flee concupiscence, to mortify carnal desires with God's help, and to await the last day and the end of labor, so that, dead to the world and living to God, they may say: But far be it from me to glory, save in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ Gal. 6.
3.29: 3.29 On the south. This signifies that after the light of knowledge has been received, the preacher ought to dispense to his neighbors, with discretion, the word of patience and consolation. Under Eleazar, that is, the help of God, according to that saying: Unless the Lord build the house, they labor in vain who build it.
3.35: 3.35 On the side. The last, the Merarites, under Ithamar, which is interpreted bitter, or where is the palm, were allotted the north side, where glacial horror endures. In this the ministers of the Church are warned not to grow numb with complacency; for although they have already entered the Church through the gate of faith, have received the light of knowledge, and have mortified the desires of the flesh, they have not yet reached perfect sweetness, that is, eternal blessedness. Something bitter remains; they must contend with him who directs his throne toward the north, whose hardness it is impossible to soften; hence: His heart shall be hardened like a stone, etc. Isa. 14; Job 21. But when he is overcome, once the palm is gained, there is cause to exult and rejoice.
3.38: 3.38 On the east side. The east side signifies the rise of faith, where Moses, interpreted taken from the water, and Aaron, mountain of strength, encamp with their sons. For those who preside in the Church, to whom the keys of the heavenly kingdom have been entrusted Matt. 6, ought to know the order of entrance and preach it to others. For everyone must enter into the light of faith through the gate of confession, to the water of baptism, so that, taken from the water, he may be a son of adoption; and, begetting sons of good work by the strength of constancy, he must diligently guard the entrance of faith through which he entered the Church, lest he be cast out idle and useless.
19.7: 19.7 And then at last, his garments washed. THE SAME. It can be understood, etc., up to rightly. But a clean man shall gather the ashes of the cow, etc. AUGUSTINE. The priest shall wash his garments, etc., up to committing it to the resurrection as to a burning.
19.8: 19.8 Until evening. THE SAME. At evening the priest enters, because the unbelieving people, which until evening, that is, the end of the world, has been placed outside the commandments of life as outside the camp, defiled with wicked works, washed with the water of baptism and penance, returns at the end of the world to the knowledge as if into the camp.
19.9: 19.9 But shall gather. AUGUSTINE. And a man shall gather together, etc., up to because outside the celebration of the Jewish custom the evangelical honor shone forth. GREGORY, Moralia, book 6, chapter 17. The priest burns the cow, a clean man gathers the ashes, because the Jew slew the weakness of the Lord, the Gentile understands his subtle mysteries. Clean are those who preach the passion of Christ to the nations. He shall pour them out. Because the Gentile does not cease to preach the sacraments which he has come to know, but makes them manifest to those who do not know. RABANUS. The clean man pours out the ashes of the cow in a most pure place when any learned man taken from the Gentiles seeks out the hearts of the Gentiles made clean by humility, and does not cease to hand on to them the mysteries of the Redeemer. When this is done, the faith of the Gentiles is multiplied, the divine power is recognized, the discipline of the precepts is held. Hence he adds, that they may be kept for the multitude of the children of Israel: for Israel is interpreted a man seeing God; and the Gentiles, well converted, are called Israel, who now contemplate God by faith. Outside the camp. Because all the Gentiles are outside the law, outside the sacrifice, outside the synagogue. Most pure. Because the secrets of the Lord's incarnation are not to be handed over to depraved and polluted minds, but to those who, coming to the faith, have cleansed their heart. For the multitude of the children. AUGUSTINE, as above. Another reading, etc., up to that, washed, he might also in some way wash his garments from the outside. For safekeeping. Because the subtler sacraments, handed over to the clean hearts of the Gentiles, are turned into fortification of the mind, because while by imitation we attend to the secret and subtle things of his working, by this we provide for ourselves against uncleanness; because of the work, may the ashes become for our safekeeping, but because of baptism, into the water of sprinkling. Then we keep the ashes carefully for our safekeeping when we consider with care our Redeemer who suffered for our iniquities. For we weigh what he will give back to the good who wished to die for the wicked, what we owe to the justice of faith, brought to his grace, we who, placed in iniquity, have received the intercession of his death.
19.10: 19.10 They shall have this. AUGUSTINE, Question 33. Another reading, etc., up to which the evening signifies.
19.11: 19.11 He who touches them. AUGUSTINE. He who touches a corpse, etc. He begins to say how men are made unclean, etc., up to I think, according to this saying through the prophet: For three and four iniquities I will not oppose.
19.12: 19.12 If on the third day, etc. THE SAME. But if he is not purified on the third day, etc., up to still, that is, even after death.
19.13: 19.13 He shall defile the tabernacle, as far as in him lies, according to that saying: Do not quench the Spirit 1 Thess. 5, though he cannot be quenched. For if he wanted it understood that the tabernacle was made unclean by this, he would command it to be cleansed.
19.15: 19.15 The vessel which, etc. RABANUS. The cover of the lid or the binding is the censure of discipline, by which whoever is not restrained is rejected as an unclean and polluted vessel. For like a vessel without a lid or binding he is defiled who, through zeal for display, lies open, covered by no veil of silence.
19.16: 19.16 AUGUSTINE, Question 34. If anyone in the field. Another reading, etc., up to that is, slain by a wound or dead without a wound.
19.19: 19.19 And he shall wash himself, etc. THE SAME. Another reading, etc., up to he shall be unclean until evening.
20.1: 20.1 And the children came, etc. ISIDORE, on Numbers, vol. 5. The thirty-third station is in the desert of Zin: this is Kadesh. Zin is interpreted holy, by antiphrasis: as a grove (lucus) is so called though it hardly gives light (luceat), or war (bellum) though it is horrible. At this station Miriam dies and is buried, signifying prophecy dead, as Moses and Aaron signify the end of the law and priesthood, who are unable to reach the promised land or lead the people out of the solitude of this world, which Jesus alone does, that is, the Savior, the Son of God. Striking with the rod. AUGUSTINE, Question 35. Because water was brought forth from the rock, etc., up to for the cross is two pieces of wood.
20.12: 20.12 Because you did not believe. ISIDORE, on Numbers. Here Moses offended the Lord, etc., up to Christ is the power of God and the wisdom of God.
20.13: 20.13 This is the water of contradiction, where the children quarreled, etc. AUGUSTINE. What is said of that water, etc., up to for of him it is said: For a sign which shall be contradicted, etc. Luke 2.
20.22: 20.22 To Mount Hor, which is on the borders. RABANUS. The thirty-fourth station is, etc., up to the ascent to paradise.
20.30: 20.30 And all the multitude. BEDE. Aaron is mourned, Jesus is not mourned, because in the law there is a descent to the underworld, in the Gospel a passage to paradise. The people wept thirty days, because before the law, under the law and under grace the synagogue does not receive spiritual joy, but sorrowfully leans over the killing letter.
21.1: 21.1 When he heard this. The Canaanite heard that Israel had come to the place of the spies, where the people once offended; he engaged in battle and led Israel captive. And again in the same place there is fighting; by vow the victor is conquered, the conquered prevail. In this it is understood that when enemies attack us, deprived of God's help, and take us captive, we should not despair: for it can happen that we conquer where we were conquered.
21.3: 21.3 Anathema. AUGUSTINE, Question 40 on Numbers. Another reading, etc., up to it is the same as I devote, I detest.
21.4: 21.4 They set out, etc. JEROME, Letter to Fabiola. The thirty-fifth station, etc., up to and with the mouth confession is made unto salvation Rom. 10.
21.8: 21.8 Make a serpent. ISIDORE, on Numbers, vol. 5. The bites of serpents were healed when the bronze serpent was lifted up and looked upon, etc., up to he lives by his divinity as the bronze.
21.10: 21.10 And the children of Israel set out and encamped, etc. The thirty-seventh station is at Oboth, which is translated magicians or soothsayers. Because after the image of God, which is shown in the reason of the heart, and the confession of faith, which is uttered by the mouth, serpents and sorcerous arts arise; but we, guarding our heart with all vigilance, let us stop our ears, lest we hear the voices of enchanters and the songs of sirens.
21.11: 21.11 From where they set out. JEROME, as above. In Iye-abarim, etc., up to this belongs properly to those who consider the rising of the sun of justice.
21.12: 21.12 They came to the torrent Zered, etc. RABANUS. The thirty-ninth station was in Dibon-gad, etc., up to but let us fear the wilderness set before us.
21.14: 21.14 In the book of the wars. AUGUSTINE, Question 42. He did not say in what book it is written, etc., up to that the war of the Lord should be written in some book of theirs.
21.16: 21.16 From that place, etc. ORIGEN, Homily 12 on Numbers. What is it that the Lord commands with such emphasis, etc., up to because the substance and nature of the Trinity is one. THE SAME, ibid. Those wells too can be seen, etc., up to and removed the earth which the Philistines had thrown in. It should be noted, however, that while Abraham lived, the Philistines did not dare to fill the wells or throw in earth, but when he was dead they grew strong and plotted against his wells, but they are restored through Isaac. Abraham's servant also found Rebecca at the wells, whose name is interpreted Patience: she becomes the wife of Isaac, but at the wells Gen. 24, 29; likewise Jacob, when he came to Mesopotamia with his father's command not to take a foreign wife, found Rachel at the wells; and Moses found Zipporah Exod. 2. If you have understood, then, what and what kind the wives of the saints are, if you wish to take patience in marriage, or wisdom and the other virtues of the soul, and to say what was said of wisdom: Her I sought to take as a wife for myself Wis. 8, be assiduous about these wells, and there you will find a spouse of this kind, because it is certain that the virtues dwell by the streams of the living word. There are therefore many wells within the soul, and very many others in the individual words and senses of the Scriptures; yet this one is more eminent, which they dug, not just any men, but princes, and the more sublime of these, whom he called kings. Therefore hymns are sung to God at this well, and it is written that this is the well of which the Lord spoke to Moses: Gather the people and I will give them water out of the well. Gather the people and I will give. The law calls you together to the well, Christ, namely the Son of God, subsisting in his own substance, yet named with the Father and the Spirit as one fountain of Godhead. To this well, then, that is, to faith in Christ, the law calls you together. Hence he himself says: for Moses wrote of me John 4. And he calls that we may drink the waters and sing him a song, that is, believe with the heart unto justice and confess with the mouth unto salvation Rom. 10. The princes dug it, and the kings hewed it out. The princes therefore dug, the kings hewed out, a word said from excudere (to hew out), not excidere (to cut off). For that is said to be hewed out which is cut or shaped in rock. The princes, then, as lesser, dug, that is, sank a certain depth as into the softness of earth; but those whom he calls kings, as stronger, penetrate not only the depth of the earth but the hardness of the rock, to reach the deeper waters and search the very veins of the abyss, knowing that the judgments of God are a great deep. These are the apostles, of whom one says: But God has revealed it to us through his Spirit; for the Spirit searches all things, even the deep things of God 1 Cor. 2. Those, then, who through the Holy Spirit can search the heights and penetrate the deep mysteries of the well are called kings, who hewed out the well in the rock, because they penetrated the hard and difficult secrets of knowledge. So the princes dug this well, and the kings of the nations hewed it out, that is, the Apostles, who gathered the nations to obey the faith, and revealed to all the knowledge of Christ, in whom are hidden all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge. For they fulfilled the command of God, teaching all nations and baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit Matt. 28. And by this they hewed out, that is, revealed, the knowledge of the well. This which we hold in our hands is also a well to us, and all the Scripture of the law and the prophets: the evangelical and apostolic together is also one well, which none can dig or hew out but kings and princes, who are able to remove the earth and take away the surface of the letter, and from the lower rock, where Christ is, bring forth spiritual senses like living water. They are called kings because they have driven out the kingdom of sin and set the kingdom of justice in their members. For it is fitting that he teach others who has first done what he teaches; hence: He who shall do and teach men so shall be called great in the kingdom of heaven Matt. 5; and to be great in the kingdom is to be a king.
21.17: 21.17 Let the well rise. ORIGEN. Begin for it the well, that is, make the well the beginning of all things, because he is the beginning and the firstborn of every creature Rev. 3. Or thus, with the words directed from the person of Moses to the people: Give a beginning to your heart, that it may begin to understand what the well is, from which spiritual waters are to be drawn, and the people of believers refreshed. Begin therefore for him, that is, for Israel, this well, so that if anyone sees the mystical sense from the heart, he may draw God from the depths. To this well Moses, that is, the law, gathers, and it seems someone comes to it, but unless he is gathered through Moses he is not acceptable to God. Marcion seems to himself to have come, and Basilides, and Valentinus: but because they did not come through Moses, nor received the law and the prophets, they cannot praise God from the fountains of Israel. Such men do not come to the well which the princes dug Gen. 14 and the kings hewed out. There is a salt valley in which there are pits of bitumen: every heresy and every sin is in a valley, and in a salt valley. For sin does not go up, but always descends to the lowest and lower places. 33.8: 33.8 At Marah, etc. THE SAME, ibid. The fifth station is Marah, etc., up to do not therefore refuse to come to bitterness.

The Red Sea, etc. JEROME, as above. In Hebrew etc., up to after they went out of Rameses.
33.11: 33.11 In the desert of Sin. JEROME, ibid. And setting out from the Red Sea they came to the desert of Sin. They arrive at it on the forty-seventh day, Scripture saying: In the third month after the going out of the children of Israel from Egypt, on this day they came into the wilderness of Sinai Exod. 19; afterward they come to the desert of Sinai. Sinai is indeed a place of the desert, which above he named Sin: but here the place of the mountain, which is in the desert itself, is rather meant, and which from the name of the desert is called Sinai. After the soul, then, has become of praiseworthy judgment and begun to have right judgment, the law is given to it by God, because it is capable of divine secrets and of heavenly visions.
33.16: 33.16 To the graves of lust, etc. JEROME. The thirteenth station, the graves of lust. This sense is from the Gospel, that the Lord Jesus, baptized, was immediately led by the Spirit into the desert and was tempted by the devil Matt. 4. So Israel, after familiar speech with God, after it had stayed near Mount Sinai for one year and four days, went out in a marvelous arrangement of camps into the wilderness of Paran, which is interpreted wild ass, or wildness; and there it succumbs to the evil beast, loathing the heavenly bread. ORIGEN. Setting out from Sinai, they come to the graves of lust, where, namely, lusts are buried and covered over, and all cupidity extinguished, that the flesh no longer lust against the spirit, being mortified by the death of Christ.
33.17: 33.17 In Hazeroth. JEROME. The fourteenth station is in Hazeroth, which is interpreted courts. There Aaron and Miriam murmur against Moses on account of the Ethiopian woman, and, in type of one murmuring against the Church gathered from the Gentiles, the people of the Jews is covered with leprosy, and does not return to the tabernacle with its former health until the appointed time of the fullness of the Gentiles is completed. ORIGEN. After this they come to Hazeroth, which is interpreted perfect courts or blessedness. Consider more carefully, traveler, what the order of advances is: after you have been buried and have mortified the lusts of the flesh, you will come to the breadths of the courts, and you will come to blessedness. For blessed is the soul that is no longer pressed by any vices of the flesh.
33.18: 33.18 In Rithmah. JEROME, as above. They encamped in Rithmah, etc., up to and let us preach the Gospel with a clear sound. ORIGEN. From there they come to Rithmah or Paran. Rithmah is interpreted consummate vision; Paran, visible mouth. What is this, but that the soul so grows that, when it ceases to be pressed by the troubles of the flesh, it has consummate visions and grasps a perfect understanding of things? knowing more deeply, namely, the causes of the incarnation of the Word of God, and the reasons of his dispensations.
33.19: 33.19 In Rimmon-perez. JEROME. Division of the pomegranate, in which the Church is signified, as many seeds covered by one rind: while it encloses the whole crowd of believers in the unity of faith. Or the variety and harmony of the virtues, hence: The multitude of believers had one heart and one soul Acts 4; and so the individual steps are divided that all are held by the same joining. ORIGEN. From there they come to Rimmon-perez, where, namely, there is a distinction of riches and heavenly things from earthly and lowest ones; for as the understanding of the soul grows, knowledge of the lofty things is given to it, and judgment is given by which it may know how to separate the eternal from the temporal, and the lasting from the perishing.
33.20: 33.20 In Libnah, etc. The brick, namely. For in this passage now we grow, now decrease, and after many advances often return to the brick, that is, carnal works. After this they come to Libnah, which is interpreted whitening. I know that in others whitening is put in a blameworthy sense, as when it is said a whitened wall, and whitened sepulchres. But here the whitening is that of which it is said: You shall wash me, and I shall be made whiter than snow Ps. 50; and, if your sins be as scarlet, I will make them white as snow. And elsewhere, They shall be whitened with snow in Zalmon. And the hair of the Ancient of Days is said to be white, that is, white like wool. This whitening is therefore understood to come from the splendor of the true light, and to descend from the clarity of heavenly visions.
33.21: 33.21 In Rissah. Bridles, namely. For if we descend to muddy works, we need to be bridled, and, wandering and headlong in our course, to be directed by the reins of the Scriptures. ORIGEN. After this there is a station in Rissah, etc., up to is therefore a visible or praiseworthy temptation.
33.23: 33.23 At Mount Shepher. JEROME. Of beauty. The mountain of beauty is Christ. The twentieth station is set at the mountain of beauty, of which it is said: Lord, who shall dwell in your tabernacle? etc. Ps. 14. You see what bridles profit: they draw us back from vices, lead us into the choirs of virtues, and make us dwell in Christ, the most beautiful mountain. ORIGEN. Another reading. From there they come to Mount Shepher, which is called sounding of the trumpet. The trumpet is the sign of war, for where the soul feels itself armed with so many and such virtues, it necessarily proceeds to war, which is against principalities and powers, and the rulers of this world. Or the trumpet sounds in the word of God, that is, of teaching and preaching: so that he who hears the trumpet may prepare himself for war.
33.24: 33.24 In Haradah. JEROME. Wonder. And note the order: after the bridles we are brought into the Church, from there we ascend to the mountain of Christ, in which, set, we marvel at what neither eye has seen nor ear heard. ORIGEN. From Mount Shepher they came to Haradah, which is interpreted made fit, that is, that he may say: He has made us fit ministers of the New Testament 1 Cor. 2.
33.25: 33.25 Makheloth. Assembly; this is the Church, of which it is said: Behold how good and how pleasant it is for brothers to dwell together in unity 1 Cor. 3. Or the harmony of all the virtues. ORIGEN. From there they come to Makheloth, which is interpreted from the beginning. For he who strives toward perfection contemplates the beginning of things, indeed refers all things to him who was in the beginning with God, and never departs from this beginning. JEROME. From this they come to Makheloth, which is rule or rods; by both power is indicated, and that the soul has advanced so far as to rule the body, as one holding the rod of power, indeed the whole world, when it says: The world is crucified to me, etc. Gal. 6.
33.26: 33.26 Tahath. Fear, which is the guardian of blessedness, that he who has ascended so high may not grow proud; as if: You have come to the Church, you have ascended to the most beautiful mountain, in your amazement and wonder you confess the greatness of Christ. You see there many companions of virtue: Do not think high thoughts, but think soberly Rom. 12. Fear is the guardian of virtues, security is slippery; hence: Your rod and your staff, they have comforted me Ps. 12. That is, while I dread torments, I keep the grace received. ORIGEN. After this there is a station at Tahath, which is confirmation or patience. For it is necessary for him who wishes to benefit others to suffer many things and bear all things patiently; hence: For I will show him how much he must suffer for my name Acts 9.
33.27: 33.27 They encamped at Terah. JEROME. That is, malice, etc., up to and Elijah is fed by ravens. ORIGEN. From there they come to Terah, which is contemplation of amazement, that is, ecstasy, when the mind is stunned with wonder at some great thing. JEROME. Terah, malice or pasture, which is referred to the leaders of the Church, or to the guarding of the soul, so that he who feeds may be careful lest the devil insinuate himself into the folds of the sheep, that is, the churches, through some hole of the vices.
33.28: 33.28 Mithkah. THE SAME. Sweetness. As if: you have ascended the high mountain of the Father, and have marveled at the choirs of virtues, you have feared ruin, you have cast out the plotters, therefore the sweet fruit of labor follows you, that the Psalmist may say: How sweet are your words to my palate! Ps. 118. Samson, who had driven birds from his fruits, and had bound the foxes that destroy vineyards, and had also slain the roaring lion, found honeycomb in the mouth of the dead. After this they came to Mithkah, which is interpreted new death: and it is a new death when we die together with Christ and are buried together, that we may live together with him.
33.29: 33.29 Hashmonah. Which is interpreted haste, because after the sweet fruits of labor we ought not to be idle, but forgetting what is past, stretch ourselves toward what is to come. ORIGEN. From there they come to Shemen, which is said to signify mouth, or bones, in which the strength and vigor of patience is declared.
33.30: 33.30 Moseroth. JEROME. Chains, or discipline. That we may wear the thresholds of the teachers; and think the precepts of the virtues and the mysteries of the Scriptures to be eternal chains against the power and chains of the devil: when these were broken Samson conquered the enemies. Of which it is said: You have broken my chains Ps. 115. He who has been bound with the chain of Christ will say: His left hand is under my head and his right hand shall embrace me Song 2. ORIGEN. From there to Moseroth, which is excluding, that he may now shut out from his thoughts the suggestions of the contrary spirit; hence: If the spirit of him that has power rise up against you, leave not your place Sir. 10. The place must therefore be held and the adversary shut out, that he may not find a place in our heart; hence: Give no place to the devil Eph. 4.
33.32: 33.32 They came to Bene-jaakan, etc. JEROME. The children of necessity or of grinding, the twenty-eighth station. Note the number, because if you begin from one and add little by little up to seven, the twenty-eighth is produced. THE SAME. Bene-jaakan is interpreted children of necessity or of grinding. Of these children it is said: Bring to the Lord the sons of rams Ps. 28. But when you have been instructed in the divine Scriptures, and know that their laws and testimonies are chains of charity, and contending with adversaries you will bind them, and bound lead them into captivity, and from enemies and captives make children of God; and the children of grinding, through fear of punishment, where there is weeping and gnashing of teeth, abandoning the chains of the devil, will bow their necks to Christ. ORIGEN. After this they come to Bene-jaakan, which signifies springs or cultivations, where, namely, he draws from the springs of divine words, until he cultivates them by drinking, so that not even the least commandment is passed over, indeed not one iota or one tittle of the word of God is held idle in his understanding. The mountain. JEROME. Hor-haggidgad or Gudgodah is interpreted messenger, or action, or cutting. For we cannot make children of necessity unless we have slain their masters, and our hand does not spare to pull the shoulder or the tip of the ear out of the lion's mouth, and we have announced the rewards to come and taught them to be girded for rebellion; hence: Cursed is he who does the work of God negligently and keeps back his sword from blood Jer. 48. And David: In the morning I put to death all the sinners of the land Ps. 100. ORIGEN. After this he comes to Gudgodah, which is interpreted testing, or crowding. A certain strength in God and bulwark is the soul's testing. For it is so mingled with the virtues that they seem to this extent neither beautiful nor full, and therefore for those setting out toward virtue there are various and frequent stations in temptations. When you have passed these, you will encamp at Jotbathah: Jotbathah is interpreted good things; to the good, therefore, one comes only after trials of temptations. Jotbathah. JEROME. Goodness, which is Christ: that when we have come to the perfect man, the priestly rank, and the age of the fullness of Christ, in which Ezekiel was by the river Chebar Ezek. 1, we may be able with David to sing in the psalm: In you, O Lord, I have hoped, let me never be put to shame Ps. 30. For the good shepherd lays down his life for his sheep. John 10.
33.34: 33.34 Abronah. THE SAME. Passage, that is, the world. For the fashion of this world passes away, and the saints coming into it desire to pass to better things. To this station comes the true Hebrew, that is, the one who passes over, who can say: Passing over, I will see this great sight Exod. 3; hence: And they who passed by did not say, The blessing of the Lord be upon you. Ps. 128. ORIGEN. From there they encamped at Abronah, which is passage: for all things must be passed over, so that even if you come to good things, you must pass to better ones, until you come to that good in which you ought always to remain.
33.35: 33.35 At Ezion-geber. JEROME. Ezion-geber, wood of a man. Because, namely, forests and all kinds of trees can figure the multitude of the nations. Up to here the solitude of Paran contains eighteen stations, which, described in the catalog, are not put in the earlier journey. ORIGEN. After this they come to Ezion-geber, which is interpreted counsels of a man. If anyone has ceased to be a boy in his thoughts, he comes to the counsels of a man, like him who said: When I became a man, I put away the things of a child 1 Cor. 13. Great, therefore, are the counsels of a man; hence: Counsel in the heart of man is like deep water. Prov. 20.
33.36: 33.36 Into the desert, etc. JEROME. It is asked, etc., up to of this station it is said: The Lord shall shake the desert of Kadesh. ORIGEN. From here again Sin, that is, temptation, because it is not otherwise expedient to make this journey. For a goldsmith, wishing to make a necessary vessel, frequently puts it to the fire, subjects it to hammers, scrapes it with files, that it may be made purer and attain the form which the craftsman has in view. THE SAME. After this they came to Paran, Kadesh, etc., up to For one dies in the valley, another in the plains, another dies on the mountain, another on the mountain of the mountain. THE SAME. From there they encamp at Mount Hor, which is interpreted mountaineer. For he comes to the mountain of God, that he may become a fertile mountain, a curdled mountain. Or, because he always dwells on the mountain of God, he may be called a mountaineer.
33.38: 33.38 Aaron the priest in, etc. ISIDORE. In the same year Aaron died in which the new people was to enter the promised land. And although on the mountain he left the priesthood to Eleazar, and the law leads those who fulfill it to the highest, yet that height itself is not beyond the streams of the Jordan, but in the extreme bounds of earthly works. And the people mourn him thirty days: Aaron is mourned, Jesus is not mourned; in the law, a descent to the underworld; in the Gospel, an ascent to paradise.
33.40: 33.40 And he heard. ISIDORE. The Canaanite also heard that Israel had come, and at the place of the spies, where he knew the people had once offended, he engaged in battle and led Israel captive. Again in the same place he is overcome, by vow the victor is conquered, the conquered prevail. By this we understand that when enemies have taken us captive, deprived of God's help, we should not despair of salvation, but fight again. It can happen that we conquer where we were conquered. And the name of that place was called Hormah, that is, anathema.
3.39: 3.39 Twenty-two thousand. The Levites are fittingly designated by the number twenty-two. For in this number are comprised the Hebrew letters, and, according to some, the books of the Old Testament. By this prescription the ministers of God are admonished to live and teach according to the law of God, and in no way to exceed it. ORIGEN, Homily 4 on Numbers. There are many differences of numbers, etc., up to the mystery of human generation is also expounded.
3.47: 3.47 Five shekels. Mystically, whoever wishes to consecrate to God the beginning of his way of life and of his will must diligently guard the five senses of the body, lest through wantonness he slip into error or unclean desires. But according to the shekel of the sanctuary, which is twenty obols, that is, according to the teaching of the Decalogue, which consists in the two precepts of charity, let him refer all his works to the house of the high priest and his sons.
4.2: 4.2 Take the sum. ORIGEN. Since the sons of Levi are divided into three orders, etc., up to and we point to those with purer senses and free from worldly things. THE SAME. Another reading, etc., up to that he may do the works in the tabernacle of the testimony.
4.3: 4.3 In the tabernacle. THE SAME. The tabernacle of the testimony, etc., up to not by the Israelites but by the Levites. And they shall wrap the ark in it. Lest perhaps some see it uncovered and die. For he who touches the ineffable sacraments is cut off, unless he has been promoted to the rank of the priesthood by merits and knowledge. ORIGEN, Homily 4 on Numbers. Seven kinds of things are enumerated, etc., up to but let others see these things covered, or rather carry them veiled on their shoulders.
4.6: 4.6 And they shall cover. The sons of Aaron, the priests, to whom it is granted to see all things bare and open.
4.7: 4.7 The bread always. AUGUSTINE, Question 7 on Numbers. And the bread that shall always be on it. Not indeed always the same loaves, but like them, because those were taken away and fresh ones were set out daily, so long as the table was never left without loaves. Therefore he said, which shall always be on it, that is, because there were always loaves, not because those loaves were always there.
4.11: 4.11 And also the altar. Another reading: and over the golden altar they shall spread a cloth of hyacinth, and they shall cover it with a covering of violet skins. This phrasing might seem absurd and incomplete, as the Latin translators wished to render it, namely over the golden altar they shall spread a cloth of hyacinth, as if it should have been said, and they shall cover the golden altar with a cloth of hyacinth, not they shall spread a cloth of hyacinth. This seems to signify that the cloth of hyacinth itself would be covered by something else. But it seems to me to be less a kind of phrasing than a somewhat obscure sense; for this can be understood: over the golden altar they shall spread a cloth of hyacinth, so that he has commanded that the cloth of hyacinth itself be covered with another thing, since the cloth was already on the altar, as if he briefly embraced both: that the altar is to be covered with a cloth of hyacinth, and the cloth of hyacinth covered with another covering. Finally he added with what he wished the cloth of hyacinth to be covered, when he added: and they shall cover it with a covering of violet skins.
4.15: 4.15 Then the sons of Kohath shall enter. ORIGEN, Homily 4. Who, though they are not priests, etc., up to whose inheritance our Lord Jesus Christ will grant us.
4.18: 4.18 Do not destroy. ORIGEN. Do not cut off the people of Kohath, etc. Understand first the placing of the tabernacle, etc., up to but they signify the works of the shoulder.
4.20: 4.20 The others none, etc. ORIGEN. In ecclesiastical observances also, etc., up to and reason has required to be brought forth into action.
4.23: 4.23 From thirty. The number thirty, which is composed of ten multiplied three times, signifies integrity of faith and perfection of work, without which no one ought to approach the divine ministries. Joseph at thirty took up the government of Egypt Gen. 11, and David, at thirty, completed the kingdom, worthy of perpetual rest 3 Kings 2. And Ezekiel at thirty merited the gifts of prophecy Ezek. 1. And because adversities ought to be borne long-sufferingly through faith, and rewards sublimely hoped for, the height of the ark or temple and the length of the tabernacle are measured in thirty cubits. Fifty, etc. ORIGEN. In this book also, concerning the spoils of enemies, etc., up to and to hand them over to the sons of Kohath to be carried on the shoulders and borne in the hands. All who enter, etc. ORIGEN, Homily 5 on Numbers. It is said of the Levites, etc., up to who is found perfect, his senses multiplied and purified in every respect.
4.35: 4.35 To the fiftieth year. ORIGEN. The fiftieth year signifies remission and indulgence, etc., up to if the completion of one decade is added, they become five hundred.
5.2: 5.2 Every leper. Lepers are the heretics, defiled by the various stains of errors, not having a uniform color of doctrine or faith; they do not hide their ignorance but display it. Indeed there is no false doctrine that does not at some time mix in something true. True things mingled with false in anyone's discussion or narrative, appearing as in the color of a single body, signify leprosy, which varies human bodies with places of true and false colors.
5.6: 5.6 A man or a woman. RABANUS on Numbers. In this chapter we are admonished that if we offend through negligence, we should wash it away by confession and penance and make restitution for the damage. If we have inflicted damage on a neighbor, let us repent before him and make restitution for the damage. But if nothing remains, let us make satisfaction to the Lord by confessing, repenting and giving alms. AUGUSTINE, etc., Question 9 on Numbers. Another reading up to which was taken away through the offense.
5.7: 5.7 They shall restore it. AUGUSTINE, Question 10 on Numbers. It is asked how it is read in Exodus, etc., up to by which a thief caught or convicted ought to be punished.
5.8: 5.8 Besides the ram. The offering of the ram signifies the passion of Christ, in which we trust most of all, because without him we can do nothing. He is the priest who reconciles us to the Father by the offering of his flesh Job 15; so we offer our gifts to him, that by his intercession we may merit pardon.
5.9: 5.9 To the priest. Namely Christ, to whom it is said: You are a priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek Ps. 109. Reserving all things to his judgment, lest perhaps one judge an uncertain matter; hence: Do not judge before the time, until the Lord comes, etc. RABANUS on Numbers. Barley meal signifies the knowledge of the old law, etc., up to is reserved to be condemned or set free.
5.15: 5.15 He shall not pour. It is not fitting that the impenitent be anointed with the oil of flattery or of indiscreet mercy, nor with the incense of superfluous praise or disordered prayer, but that vice be pursued earnestly and in due order with zeal for justice, according to the Lord's precept.
5.17: 5.17 Holy water. THE SAME. To this water the priest mixes a little earth from the floor of the tabernacle, when, by the decree of Christ, the remembrance of the patriarchs, prophets and apostles is found introduced.
5.23: 5.23 And the priest shall write in a book, etc. Because, namely, the punishment of sins is set out in Holy Scripture. Whoever drinks of it devoutly and faithfully, dreading the punishments of sins recounted in it and abstaining from sins, will find it bitterest water unto salvation. But whoever despises it, his belly swelling, his thigh will rot, and he will be a curse and an example, because he will be punished by the just judgment of God, and his own desires and deeds will be a reproach to him.
5.24: 5.24 He shall give her to drink, that her sin may be made manifest, either here for correction, or hereafter for condemnation. For there is nothing hidden that shall not be revealed Matt. 10. Hence the Lord says: The word that I have spoken to you, that will judge you on the last day John 12.
6.3: 6.3 From wine and from all that can intoxicate. RABANUS on Numbers. In the twelfth station, etc., up to and delight in the corruption of old wickedness.
6.5: 6.5 No razor shall pass. THE SAME. That is, he will retain in his mind neither guile nor malice, lest the hair of the head, that is, the thought of the mind, be defiled. But let him hold to innocence until the end of life. Otherwise the vow will not be acceptable. But he who perseveres will be saved Matt. 10.
6.6: 6.6 He shall not go in to a dead body. THE SAME. That is, he will not imitate one dead in sins, nor enter upon the life of his iniquity, lest he lose his labor. For not he who begins, but he who completes, will be crowned 2 Tim. 2.
33.41: 33.41 At Zalmonah. JEROME. They encamped at Zalmonah, etc., up to they loathe the manna, they are wounded by serpents. ORIGEN. It follows, etc., up to is Christ, and the Holy Spirit. JEROME. Zalmonah, a little image, because there the image of the Savior was expressed by the bronze serpent which hung on a pole.
33.42: 33.42 Punon. Mouth, because when we know the passion of the Son of God, what we believe with the heart we proclaim with the mouth, according to that saying: With the heart it is believed unto justice, etc. Rom. 10. ORIGEN. From here they come to Punon, which we think to be sparing of the mouth; for he who has been able to look upon the mystery of Christ and of the Holy Spirit, and has seen or heard what it is not lawful for man to utter, will of necessity have sparing of the mouth, knowing to whom, when and how one ought to speak of the divine mysteries.
33.43: 33.43 Oboth. JEROME. Magicians or soothsayers, because after the image of God which is shown in the reason of the heart, and the confession of faith which is uttered by the mouth, serpents arise and sorcerous arts provoke us to wars. But guarding our heart with all vigilance, let us stop our ears lest we hear the voices of enchanters and the songs of sirens. ORIGEN. After this they come to Oboth. Although we have not found an interpretation of this name, we do not doubt that here too, as in the others, the sequence of advances is preserved.
33.44: 33.44 On the borders. It signifies according to the letter that up to this point they were on the borders of the Edomites, and now they come to the bounds of Moab. ORIGEN. After this follows the station of Iye, that is, Chaos: for by this the progress draws near to the bosom of Abraham, who says: Between us and you a great chaos is fixed Luke 16, that he may rest with Lazarus. In Dibon-gad. JEROME. Dibon-gad, etc., up to but on the contrary let us know the wilderness set before us. ORIGEN. From there they come again to Dibon-gad, etc., up to how perfectly and piously he thinks of God is recognized.
33.46: 33.46 Almon-diblathaim. JEROME. Which is interpreted, etc., up to scarcely freed by the prayers of the people. ORIGEN. After this they come to Almon-diblathaim, which is interpreted contempt of figs, that is, where earthly things are utterly despised: for unless the things that seem to delight on earth are despised, we cannot pass to the heavenly ones.
33.47: 33.47 They came to the mountains of Abarim before Nebo, etc. JEROME. The forty-first station is translated mountains of the passers-by, and is opposite the face of Mount Nebo. ORIGEN. There follows the station Abarim, which is passage, over against Nebo, which is departure. For when the soul has passed through all these virtues and ascended to the summit of perfection, it now passes from the world and departs like Enoch, who was not found, because God took him. Even if he seems still to be in the world and to dwell in the flesh, yet he is not found in any worldly act, because God has taken him to the region of virtues. JEROME. Here Moses dies, having first seen the promised land. Nebo is interpreted conclusion, in which the law ends, and its memory is not found, but the grace of the Gospel endures without end. And it should be noted that the station of the passers-by is set in the mountains, and still needs advancement: for after the highlands we descend to the plains of Moab and the streams of the Jordan, which is interpreted descent. For nothing is so dangerous as desire for glory and boasting, and a mind puffed up with the consciousness of virtues.
33.48: 33.48 To the plains of Moab. THE SAME. In the forty-second station, etc., up to and the thorns that choked the seed of the word of God, of which it is said: I am turned in my anguish, while the thorn is fastened in me Ps. 31. ORIGEN. The last station is, etc., up to they show the progress of the mind and the increase of virtues.
33.51: 33.51 When you have crossed the Jordan, that is, when you have been baptized, as if, having put off the old man with his deeds, you have put on the new Col. 3, who is renewed in the knowledge of God.
33.52: 33.52 Destroy all. When we enter the holy land of promise by faith, let us extinguish together with idolatry also all vices. The inhabitants. The malignant spirits, the phantoms of the vices, with their suggestions; hence: Blessed is he who shall hold and dash his little ones against the rock Ps. 136.
33.54: 33.54 To the more you shall give a larger. Because those who have an abundance of virtues hope for breadth of rewards: but those who are content with few virtues receive recompense according to their merit; hence: He who sows sparingly shall also reap sparingly; and he who sows in blessings shall also reap of blessings, etc. 2 Cor. 9.
34.1: 34.1 And the Lord spoke, etc. ORIGEN, Homily 1 on Numbers. Not all are worthy of the divine numbers, etc., up to as if proceeding from the head of the apostles. The Lord spoke, then, to Moses in the desert of Sinai: those things, namely, which we briefly comprised above, where it is commanded that everyone who goes forth in the strength of Israel be numbered from twenty years old and upward, etc. If anyone, therefore, goes forth in strength, he is numbered: and not in any strength whatever, whether of the Egyptians, or Assyrians, or Greeks; but in the strength of Israel, which is taught by God through the Scriptures and handed down through apostolic and evangelical faith. ORIGEN. The reckoning of the tribes also, the distinction of orders, etc., up to so that he may belong to the Israelite number.
34.7: 34.7 To the north, etc. The Hebrews say that the northern side begins from the great sea which stretches along the shores of Palestine, Phoenicia and Syria, which is called Coele, and Cilicia, and extends through Egypt to Libya. As to what is said, reaching to the very high mountain, they claim that Mount Amanus, or the Taurus, is signified, which seems truer.
34.9: 34.9 And the borders shall go, etc. From the end of the northern side, that is, the court of Enan, the borders extend as far as Shepham, which the Hebrews call Aphamia, and from Aphamia they descend to Riblah, which is Antioch of Syria. Hence he adds, over against the fountain, which is plainly Dan, from which Antioch enjoys most abundant waters.
34.13: 34.13 This shall be the land, etc. ORIGEN. In the former division beyond the Jordan the land was divided by Moses to the two tribes of Reuben and Gad and to the half tribe of Manasseh, etc., up to and are set apart joined to the very walls. By the tall cedar, therefore, persevering contemplation is signified; by hyssop, the humility of a meek heart. For he who is raised to the heights by contemplation ought, through the compassion of humility, to condescend to those below, and not exalt himself for what he has, but gladly spend it by preaching on those who do not have it. AUGUSTINE. Another reading, etc., up to that our life may be hidden with him. RABANUS. By the cedar can be understood hope, etc., up to in us charity alone is multiplied at last. GREGORY, Moralia, book 6, chapter 17. Let it be cast into the flame, up to that in it he may learn the right works which he should do. Hyssop. ISIDORE. Baptism, because they were sprinkled with hyssop dipped in the blood of the lamb Exod. 12. And scarlet twice dyed. THE SAME. The twice-dyed scarlet is the blood of Christ, by which we are washed in mind and body. These three purge sins: the cedar, that is, faith in the cross; the hyssop, baptism or martyrdom; the scarlet, the sacrament of the Lord's blood. RABANUS. In the twice-dyed scarlet the virtue of charity is expressed, which, kindled by the flame of holy love, is commanded to be exhibited in two precepts, namely love of God and of neighbor. The twice-dyed scarlet is therefore charity formed by a double precept, that God be so loved that the neighbor is not forsaken, and the neighbor so loved that God is not despised. The priest. THE SAME. All of us who believe in Christ are priests; hence: But you are a chosen race, a royal priesthood, etc. 1 Pet. 2. The high things, then, which we perceive by contemplation, and what we do from the meekness of humility, and what we exhibit by the fire of charity, we ought to dye with the blood of the passion of Christ, so that all that is in us may imitate him from whom it is, because apart from the imitation of the passion it is not so much virtue as vice. THE SAME. This priest, who burns the flesh, skin, blood and dung of the cow, can signify the order of the Jewish priesthood together with the people beneath it consenting to the death of the Lord; hence follows: And then at last, his garments and his body washed.
